title: Rivian limits point-to-point driving to invite-only testers under NDA
key_facts: Rivian's point-to-point driving feature will first go to owners through an invitation-only 'Autonomy Early Access Program', laid out on a new Rivian support page.
It covers US R1 Gen 2 and R2 owners who pay for Autonomy+; launch is late 2026 and broad expansion not until 2027.
Invitations go to owners with an active paid subscription, heavy use of Autonomy features and a clean recent safety record.
Participants sign an NDA, enable data collection (including camera data), use features weekly, log issues and fill in monthly surveys; they are not paid.
Autonomy+ costs $2,500 once or $49.99 a month.
CEO RJ Scaringe called the first version 'Level 2++' (hands off, eyes on the road) and said eyes-off driving comes in 2027; in January 2025 he had said an eyes-free system would launch in 2026.
quote_evidence: Rivian’s point-to-point driving feature will first reach owners through an invitation-only “Autonomy Early Access Program,” and the owners it picks will have to sign a non-disclosure agreement to get in.
Rivian says point-to-point launches to that group in late 2026 and won’t expand broadly until 2027.
Autonomy+ costs $2,500 one-time or $49.99 a month
why_it_matters_hint: Shows how cautiously, and how slowly, another carmaker is rolling out Tesla-style driving help.
notes: Electrek reading of Rivian's support page. The commentary in the article is Electrek's opinion and is not used.
